actions: String-only extraction of bundled Mermaid excerpts; library and source were not executed.
Created only these new review MD/JSON files.

findings.title: Native layout-engine selector and persisted choice are missing
findings.detail: Legacy Look bar offered Standard (dagre) and ELK, registered embedded offline loaders and saved workspace state. Native controls expose neither engine nor choice; render configs do not include layout.

findings.title: Absent native layout inherits frozen Mermaid ELK default, not Standard
findings.detail: Frozen bundle has global layout elk and state-scoped layout elk. Native initialization does not override layout and registers included ELK loaders. This statically establishes configured fallback/default, not universal engine use by every diagram family. Adding dagre as a new default changes existing source-free geometry.

findings.title: Legacy engine preference and spacing metadata are not consumed by native render
findings.detail: Legacy layoutEngine is workspace state. Spacing is per-diagram layout, with density/nodeSpacing/rankSpacing and curve consumed by legacy buildMermaidConfig. Native prepare/apply uses fonts and node style fields, not imported layout or workspace layoutEngine. Main accepts layout preservation/updates, but renderer draft does not currently expose layout/engine changes.

findings.title: Present finite context drops layout and every potential new engine field
findings.detail: Saved SVG receives full diagram via main, while Present receives a finite styleKeys projection omitting layout and layoutEngine. Reusing vector.js is valuable but insufficient if input projection drops the preference. No renderer/source IPC authority should be expanded to arbitrary objects.

findings.title: Named application palettes currently collapse to light/dark for diagram rendering
findings.detail: Native shell applies named palette CSS, but Diagram and SVG pass only dark/default themes, not named themeVariables. Present hidden rendering derives appearance from system media, so a user-forced app dark/light mode can differ from Present. Imported explicit source palette handling remains in shared configureMermaidSource and should be retained.

findings.title: Legacy engine capability seed is historical and cannot qualify a new selector
findings.detail: Historical seed engine bit is live for flowchart, swimlane, ishikawa, class, state, er and requirement. Dead pairs may be remeasured by legacy idle sweep. Build seams do not include that UI closure. Seed is discovery guidance, not current hosted or native effectiveness evidence.

precedence.classification: Static inference from bundled parser and configuration code; not freshly executed fixtures.
pipeline: Mermaid preprocesses frontmatter then init/initialize directives and deep-merges directive config over frontmatter config for conflicting keys.
Source configuration is added after initialize/site configuration, with secured keys removed by Mermaid.
For theme/look/layout, diagram-scoped keys win over global keys within the selected source layer; source layer wins over initialize/UI layer; initialize layer wins over bundled defaults.
Different scoped/global paths are not a single flat last-write order: a frontmatter scoped layout can outrank a later directive global layout.
Native secure array locks securityLevel/startOnLoad/maxTextSize/maxEdges/htmlLabels/suppressErrorRendering/secure, but does not lock layout.
Unknown registered-layout resolution may fall back to dagre with a warning inside families using getRegisteredLayoutAlgorithm; requested config is not proof of effective geometry.
precedence.colourPolicy: Keep configureMermaidSource and semantic node/class colour provenance; imported theme/themeVariables/inline style/classDef continue to own their defined colours and fonts. Never regex-strip init/frontmatter or rebuild source to change UI layout.

recommendations: Add compact Layout control near preview toolbar or in a single Look disclosure, avoiding duplicate controls in global chrome and Style.
Default Auto/source, preserving current absent metadata. Show Standard/ELK as explicit finite diagram-local fallbacks only where effect is qualified.
When source declares layout, expose Source-managed state and requested algorithm; do not falsely claim ELK is effective or silently rewrite source.
Use one finite render-policy helper for preview, vector and Present, including engine default, app theme palette/mode and source precedence.

Choose one strict new diagram engine scalar contract (dagre/elk, absent means inherited), add it to draft validation/history/reset, main typed patch, import validation and Present projection; never repurpose existing layout object without updating its sanitizer.
Do not bulk-migrate legacy workspace layoutEngine into every diagram. If offered, make migration explicit and preserve original workspace preference.

Resolve appearance in main from the actual application preference or a finite saved rendering policy; pass identical resolved light/dark/palette into SVG and Present instead of using hidden renderer system media.
Retain saved-version/hash checks, public/private projection boundaries, offline CSP, serial rendering, imported colours and explicit Save behavior.

After approved implementation, qualify source/frontmatter/init precedence; no-source Auto/Standard/ELK; nested dense graphs; actual effective engine change; saved SVG/Present parity; Lock/pending style/history; and source colours across named palettes. Existing 28-source render coverage alone is not an engine-pair qualification.
limits: No engine geometry/effectiveness, colour fidelity, performance or native UX result was measured.
Current CI status was supplied by parent and not fetched or changed here.
Findings describe inspected source at recorded hashes, not a released build or new PASS verdict.

Final 10:56 readback found five concurrent source changes while root began the approved layout extension. Earlier hashes remain the inspected preflight snapshot; this report does not qualify those later versions. No audited product source was changed by this reviewer.
